Sachar Committee Report on state of Muslims 
*161.  SHRI B. K. HARIPRASAD: 
SHRI PRAVEEN RASHTRAPAL: 
Will the Minister of MINORITY AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a)whether Government have examined the Sachar Committ ee's report 
on the state of Muslims in India; 
(b)if so, the salient findings of the Sachar Committee; and 
(c) whether a similar Committee headed by Dr. Gopal Sin gh was 
appointed two and a half decades ago by Government to access the social and 
economic status of Muslims and if so, the action ta ken on its report by 
Government? 
THE MINISTER OF MINORITY AFFAIRS (SHRI A. R. 
ANTULAY): (a) and (b) The report of the Prime Minis ter's High Level 
Committee on the Social, Economic and Educational s tatus of the Muslim 
Community of India, under the chairmanship of Justi ce Rajinder Sachar, has 
been tabled in the Rajya Sabha on 30.11.2006. The report is being examined. 
(c) The Government constituted a High Power Panel o n 10th May, 
1980 and it submitted its Report on Minorities, S.C ., S.T. and Weaker 
Sections. This was initially heades by Dr. V. A. Se yid Mohammad, who 
resigned in early September 1980 to take up another  assignment and was 
taken over by Dr. Gopal Singh. The report alongwith  a statement indicating 
the comments of the Government on the recommendatio ns made by this 
panel was laid on the table of Rajya Sabha on 24th August, 1990. 
Sale of Dabhol Power Plant

to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Government have received suggestions for 
selling of Dabhol Power Plant; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) the reasons therefor; and 
(d) the steps Government are taking in this regard? 
THE MINISTER OF POWER (SHRI SUSHIL KUMAR SHINDE): ( a) 
No, Sir. There is no such proposal with the Governm ent for sale of Dabhol 
Power Plant at Ratnagiri. 
(b) to (d) Do not arise.

Achievements of Science and Technology  
†*166. SHRI MANGANI LAL MANDAL: Will the Minister o f 
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that achievement and progress in the field of 
science and technology of India is not encouraging; 
(b) whether it is also a fact that the standard and qua lity of research-
work is constantly on the decline due to lack of es sential and favourable 
coordination between education and research in the country; 
(c) whether it is also a fact that India is even laggin g far behind 
compared to South Korea, China and other developing  countries due to 
decline in the standard and quality of research-work; and 
(d) if so, the reasons therefor and the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY (SHRI KAPIL 
SIBAL): (a) to (d) India's progress and achievement s in the field of science 
and technology vary in different sectors. In areas such as Space Science, 
Information Technology and Bio Technology, India is  seen by the global 
community as an emerging R&D hub. The standard and quality of basic 
research as reflected by research papers published in SCI journals has been 
increasing in absolute terms over the past 25 years  from 14983 in 1980 to 
19448 in 2005. However the share of India as percen tage of world 
publications declined from 2.9% in 1980 to 1.5% in 1995 and then gradually 
increased to 1.9% in 2005. One of the parameters me asured in global science 
and technology for assessing the quality of publications is the average impact 
factor per publication. This has registered an incr ease from 0.748 in 1985-86 
to 1.229 in 2001-02. Its share of top 1 % highly ci ted publications also 
increased from 0.32 in 1993-97 to 0.54 in 1997-2001 . Even the number of 
US patents granted to Indian inventors has been inc reasing—from 88 in 
2000-01 to 229 in 2004-05. Other countries like Chi na and South Korea, 
however, have progressed much faster. South Korea a nd China received 
private sector contribution to the tune of 60-65% of the total outlay for R&D. 
Public-Private-Partnership in R&D support in S.Kore a and China is 
significant. In India, private sector contribution to overall R&D outlay is 
only to the tune of 25% of the total outlay. The nu mber of scientists per 
thousand population in China is about 6 times 
†Original notice of the question was received in Hindi.  
26 

[4 December, 2006] RAJYA SABHA 
that of India. Therefore, China may have higher quantum of papers but India 
does not suffer from quality shortfalls. 
While centrally funded research institutions and so me central 
universities are doing internationally competitive research, state of research 
in most other universities is highly unsatisfactory . Universities are the 
mainstay of scientific research all over the world,  but, in our country, 
universities have been suffering because of a varie ty of financial and 
governance problems leading to, among other things,  depletion of faculty, 
impoverishment of research infrastructure and lack of opportunities for the 
faculty for updating their knowledge. Most universi ties fall in the domain of 
State Governments and they need to address the prob lems urgently. Among 
other things, there is a need to increase the fundi ng for research and teaching 
in educational institutions. 
The Government of India, on its part, has taken a n umber of steps to 
rejuvenate and promote scientific research in unive rsities and other scientific 
institutes of excellence. The Plan Allocation of sc ientific departments has 
been doubled from about Rs. 12000 crore in the Nint h Plan to about Rs. 
25000 crore in the Tenth Plan. Eleventh Plan progra mme for science & 
technology seeks significant increase in the budget  outlay. The Research 
Infrastructure programme of DST is a targeted progr amme to upgrade the 
laboratory infrastructure in universities and other  higher educational 
institutions. Several institutions, centres of exce llence and facilities in 
emerging and frontline areas have also been establi shed; for example, in the 
areas of Brain Research, Marine Biotechnology, Stem  Cell and Tissue 
Engineering, Soft Computing, Water Resources Develo pment, 
Nanophosphors, Display Technology, Fuel Cell Techno logy Ultrafast 
Proceses, Protein Research, etc. More recently, two  new Indian Institutes of 
Science Education and Research (IISERs) have been s et up at Kolkata and 
Pune which, apart from carrying out frontline and i nternationally competitive 
research, would offer M.Sc. programmes in a multi-d isciplinary and 
academically flexible and research-oriented environ ment. Various agencies 
of Government of India have now attractive scholars hip, fellowship and 
research support schemes for scientifitic manpower of all ages starting right 
from the school level.

Assessment of global warming on Indian climates 
1175. SHRI RAHUL BAJAJ: Will the Minister of EARTH 
SCIENCES be pleased to state: 
(a) whether an assessment of likely impact of global wa rming on 
Indian climate has been made; 
(b) if so, what are its major findings; and 
(c) if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF EARTH SCIENCES (SHRI KAPIL SlBAL): (a) 
Yes, Sir. 
(b) Impact of global warming on future climate chan ge in India have 
been evaluated by Indian scientists through climate  predictions based on 
different scenarios of global trends in Greenhouse gas emissions, which have 
been agreed to by the Inter Governmental panel on c limate change. The 
results are obtained from Global Model simulations followed by Regional 
simulations to get results relevant to the Indian r egion. It must however be 
noted that these results can only be considered as preliminary at the present 
stage and efforts are being continued by the scient ific community to obtain 
more reliable estimates. 
In the case of mean annual temperature for the coun try as a whole, an 
increase of the order of 2 oc to 5°c is projected to occur by the end of this 
century based on the model results. Examination of the spatial patterns of 
annual temperature changes indicates that the warmi ng will be more 
pronounced over the northern States of India and ea stern parts of the 
peninsular region, it is estimated to be more durin g winter and post monsoon 
seasons compared to the rest of the year. 
Prediction of rainfall changes is less reliable tha n that of temperature. 
The global results indicate that there is likelihoo d of increase in annual mean 
rainfall to the tune of 15-40 per cent till the end  of the 21st century as 
compared to the baseline period 1961-1990. The maxi mum change in rainfall 
is projected to occur over the climatologicaily low  rainfall region of north-
western India. Considering monsoon season separatel y a decrease in rainfall 
in the western parts of the country and a correspon ding increase in the 
eastern parts is projected. 
The Central and western parts of the country show a  reduction in the 
number of rainy days by middle of present century i ndicating that heavier 
precipitation events could become slightly more fre quent in the non monsoon 
months

to the predicted mode! results but the rainfall dat a does not show any

Causes of power crisis in the capital 
* 1277. SHRIMATI HEMA MALINI: Will the Minister of POWER be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the present mess on the p ower front in the 
capital is due to lack of advance planning to tie u p with the neighbouring 
States on time and proper assessment of power requirements for summer; and 
(b) if so, the details of the steps Government have tak en to face the 
mess on power front in the capital? 
THE MINISTER OF POWER (SHRI SUSHIL KUMAR SHINDE): ( a) 
There is overall shortage of power in the country. During the period April—
October, 2006 in the current year (2006-07), the av erage energy and peak 
shortage in the country was 8% and 12% respectively . In comparison the 
energy shortage and peak shortage in Delhi was 2.4%  and 6.6.% respectively. 
However, Delhi experiences power shortage during pe ak summer and peak 
winter months especially during morning and evening  peak hours when the 
load increases sharply. Advance planning is done by  Delhi Transco Ltd. to 
arrange power for meeting the anticipated deficit i n general and particularly 
by the peak summer as well as peak winter months. 
However, higher shortages were witnessed during cer tain periods in 
the peak summer of 2006 due to unscheduled outage o f generating units and 
short supply of gas due to floods in Gujarat. 
(b) Following measures have been taken/are being ta ken by 
Government to meet power shortages in Delhi: 
e In addition to firm share, allocation of power fr om unallocated quota 
in CGSs in Northern Region (NR) has been made to De lhi on time 
slot basis according to demand pattern. 
e Delhi would get additional power from following u pcoming projects 
of Tehri HEP (4x250 MW), Dulhasti HEP (3x130 MW) an d Tala 
HEP (6x170 MW). While, two units of Tehri HEP have been 
commissioned, benefits from other units of aforesai d projects are 
likely to accrue in the current financial year. 
• Moll has been signed by Delhi Transco Ltd. (DTL) with NTPC to 
augment the capacity by 980 MW (2x490 MW) in Badarp ur

willing to buy power at the rate at which this project will be able to offer.

130,0. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA: Will the Minister of SC IENCE

(a) whether Indian Sub-group on Clinical Research and T ransfer of Bio-
materials under Indo-US Joint Industry Working Grou p on biotechnology 
recommended for a new drug authority body on the lines of TRAI and IRDA;

technology sector;

1) A single window clearance mechanism with standard 
operating procedures (SOPs) for import and export o f 
biologicals; clinical trial and pharmacogenomic sam ples and 
export of Special Chemicals, Organisms, Materials, 
Equipments Technologies (SCOMET) items.

AND EMPOWERMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that there are over 77 million  senior citizens in 
the country who may account for 301 million—17 per cent of our population 
by 2051 and who cast 24 per cent of the total votes during the elections;

which will constitute 21 % of the total population at that time. The data 
regarding total votes cast by senior citizens is not available.

THE MINISTER OF TRIBAL AFFAIRS (SHRI P.R. KYNDIAH):  (a) 
The total number of tribals in the country as per P opulation Census 2001 is 
84,326,240. The State-wise details of the people am ong them living below 
the poverty line are given in Statement (See below). 
(b) Different Sectoral Ministries under the Central  Government cover 
tribals as well as other people under their program mes. As far as programmes 
meant exclusively for tribals are concerned, the fo llowing are being 
implemented by Ministry of Tribal Affairs; 
Central Sector Schemes 
(i) Grant-in-aid to NGOs for Scheduled Tribes inclu ding Coaching 
and Allied and award for exemplary service: 
Funds are released for preparing ST candidates for competitive 
examinations to improve their representation in var ious posts and 
services. 
(ii) Vocational Training in Tribal Areas: The schem e aims at 
developing the skills of the tribal youth for gainf ul employment/ 
self employment. 
(iii) Educational Complex in Low Literacy Pockets: Funds are provided 
for improving literacy among ST women in districts with less than 
10% of female literacy. 
(iv) Grant-in-Aid to State Tribal Development Coope rative 
Corporations for Minor Forest Produce: Support is g iven to Tribal 
Development Cooperative Corporations, Minor Forest Produce 
Trade and Development Federations or Forest Develop ment 
Corporations in the States for dealing with Minor F orest Produce 
items. 
(v) Development of Primitive Tribal Groups (PTGs): Funds are 
provided for any activity to be undertaken for the benefit of the 
PTGs. 
(vi) Rajiv Gandhi National Fellowship (RGNF) for ST 
students: Fellowships are provided to ST students t o enable them 
to pursue higher studies for obtaining M.Phil and P h.D 
qualifications.

Centrally-Sponsored Schemes 
(vii) Scheme of Post Matric, Book Bank & Upgradatio n of Merit of 
Scheduled Tribe Students: Post Matric Scholarships are sanctioned 
to ST students, books are supplied to ST students p ursuing 
professional courses and upgradation of merit of ST students. 
(viii) Girls and Boys Hostels for Scheduled Tribes:  Funds are provided 
to States/UTs for construction of new hostel buildi ngs and/or 
extension of existing hostels. 
(ix) Ashram Schools in Tribal Sub-Plan Areas: Funds  are provided for 
establishment of residential schools for ST boys and girls. 
(x) Research Information & Mass Education, Tribal F estival end 
Others: Grants are given for Research Fellowships, Tribal 
Research Institutes (TRIs) set up in the States/UTs , research and 
evaluation projects, seminars and publications. 
Special Area Programmes 
(xi) Special Central Assistance to Tribal Sub-Plan:  Special Central 
Assistance is provided to Tribal Sub-Plan States fo r filling up the 
critical gaps in employment-cum-incoms generation a ctivities and 
infrastructure incidental thereto. 
(xii) Grants-in-aid under Article 275(1) of the Con stitution: Funds are 
released for providing infrastructure to Tribal Wel fare Educational 
Institutions. 
The Ministry of Tribal Affairs disseminates information about its 
schemes/programmes to the tribals through the following measures: 
(i) A quarterly Newsletter 'Janjatiya Jagran', publ ished by this

ST population. 
(ii) Documentary films made on various aspects of t ribal life and 
telecast through Doordarshan, on a weekly basis.

(iv) The Ministry's website which contains details of programmes/ 
activities and the Annual Report of the Ministry.

the year 2003-04 at primary level is 91.37% and upp er primary level is

Children suffering from malnutrition  
1324. SHRI S.S. AHLUWALIA: Will the Minister of WOM EN AND 
CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have conducted any scientific st udy/survey to 
ascertain the size of population of children suffer ing from malnourishment 
owing to poverty in various parts of the country; 
(b) if so, the State-wise details thereof; 
(c) if not, the reasons therefor; 
(d) whether Government contemplate to conduct a special  study for 
this purpose in the near future; and 
(e) if not, the rationale thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN 
AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT (SHRIMATI RENUKA CHOWDHURY): 
(a) to (c) Yes, Sir. The National Family Health Sur veys (NFHS)-1 conducted 
during 1992-93 and NFHS 2 conducted during 1998-99 by the International 
Institute of Population Sciences, Mumbai, under the  aegis of Ministry of 
Health and Family Welfare, included assessment of m agnitude of 
malnutrition amongst children below three years in major States of the 
country. NFHS-2 Report also analyses the extent of malnutrition amongst 
children on the basis of standard of living index of the family. 
State-wise details on prevalence of malnutrition am ongst children 
below three years are given in the enclosed statement (See below). 
(d) and (e) NFHS-3 has already been undertaken in t he country during 
2005-06. Provisional data for some States has since  been released during 
August and November, 2006 and the provisional data in respect of remaining 
major States would be available shortly. Complete r eport of NFHS-3 would 
be available in due course.

Incentives for girl child  
1326. SHRI S. ANBALAGAN: Will the Minister of WOMEN  AND 
CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government are aware that girl child is  still not the 
automatic choice of parents in the country; 
.      (b) if so, the concrete steps proposed to be taken to adopt stick and carrot 
policy towards parents to ensure well being of girl child; and 
(c) the steps proposed to be taken by Government to  prevent female 
foeticide and girl child discrimination? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN 
AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT (SHRIMATI RENUKA CHOWDHURY) 
(a) Yes, Sir. 
(b) and (c) The Ministry of Health and Family Welfa re, in order to 
check female foeticide, implements the Prenatal Dia gnostic Technique 
(Regulation and Prevention of Misuse) Act, 1994 (am ended in 2003). The 
Act prohibits determination and disclosure of the s ex of the foetus. Under 
the Act, use of Pre-natal diagnostic Techniques and  genetic counseling is 
permissible for detection of genetic abnormalities.  The violation of the Act 
is punishable with imprisonment upto 5 years and fi ne upto Rs. 1.00 lakh 
apart from cancallation of registration and license . Steps are also taken 
for creation of awareness against the practice of p re-natal determination of 
sex through radio, television and print media units ; constitution of a National 
Monitoring and Inspection Committee which has repre sentatives from 
National Commission for Women and Ministry of Women  and Child 
Development takes stock of the ground realities by field visits to the problem 
States; setting up of a National Surveillance Cell for effective 
implementation 
240 

[4 December, 2006] RAJYA SABHA 
of the Act; and sensitization of the Medical Commun ity, Police and Training 
of Judiciary. In addition, other activities underta ken are sensitization of the 
organizations working against sex selection, involv ement of the medical 
professionals, religious/spiritual leaders to spread the message. 
The Working Group on 'Development of Children' for the Eleventh 
Five Year Plan (2007-2012) has been constituted by the Planning 
Commission in April, 2006. The deliberations of the  Working Group will 
serve as an input into the Steering Committee Repor t of the Planning 
Commission. The recommendations of the Steering Com mittee would from 
the basis for the programmes and schemes for the gi rl child of the Ministry 
of Women and Child Development in Eleventh Plan.

1327. SHRI JANARDHANA POOJARY: Will the Minister of  
WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of 'Integrated Child Development Scheme ' (ICDS) with 
allocation made and spent, number of beneficiary ch ildren for the last three 
years, year-wise and State-wise; 
(b) whether implementation of various welfare measures under the 
ICDS is not effective at the State level in the abs ence of proper monitoring 
system; 
(c) if so, the details thereof; 
(d) whether the level of malnutrition among the rural c hildren has not 
declined despite claims of providing nutritious mea l under the mid-day meal 
scheme; and 
(e) if so, the measures proposed to be taken to ensure proper 
implementation of the ICDS, particularly the mid-day meal programme? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN 
AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT (SHRIMATI RENUKA CHOWDHURY): 
(a) Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) Sc heme was launched in 
1975 in 33 Community Development Blocks. The Scheme  was gradually 
expanded and today it covers 6118 blocks in the cou ntry including 4790 in 
rural areas, 805 in tribal areas and 523 in urban slums. The services provided

supplementary nutrition, immunization, referral ser vices, health check-up, 
pre-school non-formal education and nutrition and h ealth education. The

and its supplementary nutrition component are given  in Statements-I and 
Statement-ll respectively (See below). Number of be neficiary, State-wise, of 
supplementary nutrition and Pre-school Education is  given in the Statement-
Ill and Statement-IV respectively (See below). 
(b) and (c) ICDS is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme im plemented 
through the State Governments/Union Territory (UT) Administrations. 
Government of India has prescribed the records and registers to be 
maintained at Anganwadi level; Progress Reports for mats for Child 
Development Project Officer (CDPO) at block level; and consolidated 
reporting formats at State level to capture informa tion on various important 
aspects of the Scheme. Various quantitative inputs captured through CDPO's 
Progress reports are compiled at the State level. N o instance of absence of 
monitoring in a State/UT has come to the notice of the Government. 
(d) Cooked Mid-Day Meal Programme (MDM) was launched w.e.f. 
September, 2004 for children studying at Primary st age in Government and 
Government assisted schools and Centres run under E ducation Guarantee 
Scheme and Alternative and Innovative Education (EG S &AIE). Under the 
Programme, mid-day meal of minimum 300 calories wit h 8-12 grams of 
protein was prescribed. No baseline information on nutritional status of such 
children is available with the Government.
